key_concepts: Heat transfer occurs through conduction, convection, and radiation
Conduction involves heat transfer through a conductor like a metal spoon
Wood and plastic are poor conductors or insulators of heat
In convection, hot water rises while cold water sinks
Radiation can transfer heat and cause ice cream to melt
Heat moves from warmer objects to cooler objects
Rubbing two objects transfers electrons and produces opposite charges
Charging by friction occurs when two objects are rubbed together
Charging by conduction occurs when a charged body touches a neutral body
A negatively charged balloon near a can pushes electrons away, causing attraction
Touching the can with a finger allows electrons to flow out, leaving it positively charged
Static electricity can attract hair, separate pepper and salt, and make plates repel
